cls: Gastroprotective mucosal agent (amino acid analog of 2(1H)-quinolinone)
pharm: Stimulates endogenous prostaglandin synthesis and gastric mucus/bicarbonate secretion, scavenges free radicals, and promotes mucosal blood flow and epithelial repair.

May be taken with or without food; commonly after meals and at bedtime
Safety not established; use only if benefit outweighs risk (per SmPC/PI)
Animal data show milk excretion; avoid or discontinue nursing
Largely renally excreted; use with caution in renal impairment
No specific adjustment established; use with caution
Avoid excess alcohol which aggravates gastric mucosal injury
Symptom response; rare hepatic enzyme rise or blood count changes
summary: Rebamipide is a gastroprotective (mucosal cytoprotective) agent that is NOT FDA-approved; it is approved and widely used in Japan and several Asian countries (e.g., as Mucosta) for gastric ulcers and for gastric mucosal lesions in acute and chronic gastritis. Rather than suppressing acid, it enhances mucosal defense by increasing gastric prostaglandin synthesis, mucus and bicarbonate secretion, and mucosal blood flow, while scavenging reactive oxygen species and promoting epithelial repair. It is generally very well tolerated, with rare hypersensitivity, hepatic enzyme elevation, and blood dyscrasias reported.
indications: Improvement of gastric mucosal lesions (erosion, bleeding, redness, edema) in acute gastritis and acute exacerbation of chronic gastritis
Adjunct to reduce NSAID-induced gastrointestinal mucosal injury and as an ophthalmic preparation for dry eye in some countries (clinical/off-label uses)

moa: Rebamipide protects and heals the gastrointestinal mucosa through several actions rather than acid suppression. It stimulates endogenous prostaglandin (PGE2 and PGI2) synthesis in the gastric mucosa, increasing secretion of protective mucus and bicarbonate and enhancing mucosal blood flow. It scavenges reactive oxygen species and inhibits neutrophil-mediated inflammation, and it promotes epithelial cell proliferation and migration, accelerating ulcer healing and restoring the mucosal barrier.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to rebamipide or any component
relative: Significant renal impairment (drug is renally eliminated)
monitor: Liver function and blood counts if reactions are suspected

preg: The safety of rebamipide in pregnancy has not been established; it should be used during pregnancy only when the expected benefit outweighs the potential risk, in line with the prescribing information.
lact: Animal studies have shown excretion into milk; breastfeeding should be avoided during treatment, or the drug discontinued, because safety in nursing infants is not established.
renal: Rebamipide and its metabolites are excreted mainly by the kidneys, so plasma exposure may increase in renal impairment; use with caution and monitor, particularly in the elderly.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is defined for hepatic impairment; rare elevations of hepatic enzymes and jaundice have been reported, so monitor liver function if clinically indicated.

moderate: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interactions are well established; data are limited
minor: May be combined with acid-suppressing therapy (PPIs/H2 blockers) without known adverse interaction
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Excess alcohol aggravates gastric mucosal injury and should be limited.
interactions.diagnostics: Rarely associated with elevated hepatic transaminases or altered blood counts on laboratory testing.

monitoring: Liver function tests if hepatic reaction suspected
Complete blood count if blood dyscrasia suspected

pearls: Not FDA-approved; approved and widely used in Japan and parts of Asia as Mucosta - information is based on the Japanese prescribing information/SmPC, not an FDA label
Acts by boosting mucosal defense (prostaglandins, mucus/bicarbonate, blood flow) and scavenging free radicals - not an acid suppressant
Commonly combined with PPIs and used to mitigate NSAID-induced GI injury
Also formulated as an ophthalmic suspension for dry eye in some countries
Very well tolerated overall; serious reactions (hepatic, hematologic) are rare
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the usual three-times-daily schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Experience with rebamipide overdose is limited, and its toxicity is low. Management is supportive and symptomatic; there is no specific antidote.
